column1:
Incorporating Beige Book insights alongside SLOOS tilts the June 12 FOMC statement toward a more cautious read than policy communications alone.

- Policy stance: The FOMC maintained a restrictive setting (5.25–5.50% target range, ongoing QT with $25B Treasuries/$35B MBS caps; IORB at 5.4%, ON RRP at 5.3%), reiterating no cuts until greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably to 2%.
- Beige Book overlay: District reports point to economic activity that is slight-to-modest overall rather than “solid” everywhere, with mixed consumer spending and more price sensitivity as consumers push back on higher prices. Labor market conditions remain generally tight but hiring expectations have softened, and wage growth is moderating toward pre‑pandemic norms. Prices are still rising across districts but at a slower pace.
- SLOOS overlay: Banks tightened standards and terms for C&I, consumer, and especially CRE loans; demand softened across these categories. Reported drivers include a weaker outlook, reduced risk tolerance, liquidity considerations, and property-market concerns.
- Implications: The combination of tighter credit supply, softer loan demand, moderating wage growth, and greater consumer price resistance adds headwinds to growth while supporting gradual disinflation. This raises downside risks to activity (notably in CRE) even as inflation shows modest further progress.
- Net read-through: Relative to the FOMC’s “solid pace” characterization, the Beige Book and SLOOS pull the tone closer to neutral/slightly positive with an emphasis on caution and patience.
